articles.title: Boi Caprichoso anuncia tema para o Festival de Parintins 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Anúncio foi feito durante a festa de aniversário do bumbá, realizada neste sábado (31), no Curral Zeca Xibelão, em Parintins.
articles.summary: Boi Caprichoso celebra 113 anos e anuncia "Criação que vem da alma" como tema para o Festival de Parintins 2027, exaltando a ancestralidade e a cultura da ilha.
articles.body:
Boi Caprichoso anuncia tema para o Festival de Parintins 2027 — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O Boi-Bumbá Caprichoso celebrou 113 anos neste sábado (31), em Parintins , no interior do Amazonas, e anunciou o tema que vai marcar sua apresentação no Festival de Parintins 2027: "Criação que vem da alma". A festa de aniversário foi realizada no Curral Zeca Xibelão e reuniu torcedores e integrantes do bumbá.

Fundado em 20 de outubro de 1913, o Caprichoso completou 113 anos no último dia 20, mas a comemoração oficial foi realizada neste sábado.

Segundo o Conselho de Arte do boi, o tema escolhido destaca a cultura e os saberes do povo de Parintins, além das tradições e influências que formam a identidade da ilha.

A proposta também valoriza a ancestralidade indígena e africana, as manifestações culturais, a natureza amazônica e as histórias transmitidas entre gerações.

Em uma publicação nas redes sociais, o Caprichoso apresentou o conceito do tema e destacou a relação do boi com a história e a identidade da população parintinense.

"Eu sou a luta de um povo, carrego nas veias a história e trago na alma a criação dos nossos sonhos mais bonitos", diz um trecho da publicação.

No texto de apresentação do tema, o Conselho de Arte também descreve o Caprichoso como uma criação coletiva, construída pelas mãos de artistas, trabalhadores e moradores de Parintins.

"É o Caprichoso, o boi do povo, das lutas, do afeto, da ternura das crianças e da garra dos bravos paikicés, da batida forte do treme-terra e da leveza da poesia da toada. É a manifestação viva da essência de um povo. É o Caprichoso: Criação Que Vem da Alma".

O tema será desenvolvido nas apresentações do bumbá durante o Festival de Parintins 2027.

articles.title: Gabriel O Pensador lança álbum ao vivo gravado há um ano em show no Rio com Ben Jor, Jota.Pê, Mano Brown e Rael | G1
articles.body:
Capa do álbum 'Acústico 33 anos', de Gabriel O Pensador — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Em 3 de dezembro de 2025, Gabriel O Pensador fez show retrospectivo no palco da Fundição Progresso, no Centro da cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ), com sucessos reunidos pelo rapper carioca em 33 anos de carreira iniciada em 1992 com a explosão nas rádios do rap “Tô feliz (Matei o presidente)”.

O show foi gravado ao vivo para gerar registro audiovisual que chega enfim ao mercado fonográfico quase um após a captação do espetáculo apresentado pelo Pensador com time estelar de convidados que incluiu Jorge Ben Jor , Jota.Pê, Rael, Lulu Santos, MV Bill e Mano Brown, entre outros nomes.

Nos aplicativos de áudio a partir da próxima sexta-feira, 6 de novembro, o álbum “Acústico 33 anos” alinha 17 faixas, sendo que somente uma delas – o medley com “Pátria que me pariu” e “Capítulo 4, versículo 3”, gravado pelo Pensador com Mano Brown, voz do grupo Racionais MC's – foi adiantada em single editado em 6 de agosto.

Aberto por “Até quando?” (Gabriel o Pensador, Tiago Mocotó e Itaal Shur, 2001), rap de pegada roqueira que marcou a discografia do artista carioca há 25 anos, o álbum “Acústico 33 anos” fecha com “2345meia78”, megahit do álbum mais pop do Pensador, “Quebra-cabeça” (1997).

Ao longo das 17 faixas do álbum “Acústico 33 anos”, Gabriel O Pensador faz “Lavagem cerebral” com MV Bill, recicla “Mandei avisar” com Jota.Pê, divide “Cachimbo da paz” com Lulu Santos, repisa “Caminhando a pé” com Rael, canta “Reggae do marasmo” com Ventania, faz feat com Tiago Mocotó em “Pega ladrão!”, reedita o dueto de 2012 com Jorge Benjor em “Solitário surfista / Surfista solitário” e incursiona pelo repertório do grupo Charlie Brown Jr. em “Zóio de lula” (1999).

articles.title: Anelis Assumpção mergulha no reggae em álbum com Alice Carvalho, Liniker, Tetê Espíndola e Thalma de Freitas | G1
articles.body:
Capa do álbum 'Anelis e o favo favorito', de Anelis Assumpção — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Novembro chega com o quinto álbum de estúdio de Anelis Assumpção , “Anelis e o favo favorito”. Invertendo a ordem habitual adotada pelo mercado fonográfico, o álbum é lançado primeiramente em LP – com vinil fabricado na cor mel, em afinidade com o título – e somente em 30 de novembro ficará disponível em edição digital nos aplicativos de áudio.

Em “Anelis e o favo favorito”, a artista dá um mergulho mais profundo na praia do reggae – gênero recorrente na discografia da cantora – em álbum que flerta com a cultura do Sound System e que apresenta repertório essencialmente inédito e autoral, gravado com participações de Alice Carvalho, Bento Assumpção, Gracê Passô, Liniker, Rubi, Tetê Espíndola e Thalma de Freitas. Alice Carvalho tambassina texto escrito para a edição em LP.

A produção musical do álbum “Anelis e o favo favorito” foi orquestrada pela própria Anelis Assumpção em parceria com Curumin, Ed Trombone e Saulo Duarte, este também parceiro da artista na composição de várias músicas do disco.

“Anelis e o favo favorito” chega ao mundo 15 anos após o primeiro álbum solo da cantora, “Sou suspeita, estou sujeita, não sou santa” (2011), ao qual se seguiram “Anelis Assumpção e os amigos imaginários” (2014), “Taurina” (2018) e “Sal” (2022).

articles.title: Natascha Falcão lança música gravada para trilha da novela 'Lá na minha terra' | G1
articles.body:
Natascha Falcão canta a música inédita 'Desafio de amar' na trilha sonora da novela 'Lá na minha terra' — Foto: Maria Magalhães / Divulgação

♬ Em cena desde 2006, primeiramente como atriz e depois como cantora, Natascha Falcão chega aos 20 anos de carreira com crescente visibilidade nacional. E a projeção da artista pernambucana tende a aumentar a partir de 9 de novembro, data da estreia da próxima novela das 18h da TV Globo, “Lá na minha terra”.

É que Natascha gravou uma das principais músicas da trilha sonora orquestrada sob direção musical de Daniel Tauszig e Ricardo Leão para a trama ambientada entre a fictícia cidade nordestina de Lavra Seca e a capital de São Paulo.

Já em rotação nas chamadas da novela, a música é inédita, se chama “Desafio de amar” e tem letra escrita com versos alusivos ao drama romântico da protagonista da trama, Rosenda (Dira Paes), mulher abandonada em Lavra Seca pelo marido Severino (Daniel de Oliveira), que foi para São Paulo (SP) e lá trocou de identidade e casou de novo.

A gravação de “Desafio de amar” por Natascha Falcão será lançada em single programado para chegar aos aplicativos de áudio em 9 de novembro, dia da estreia da novela “Lá na minha terra”.

articles.title: Rajpal Yadav breaks down as Bollywood bids farewell to Sanjay Gupta, says death is 'shocking... no words'
articles.summary: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta, known for 'Kaante', 'Shootout at Lokhandwala' and 'Kaabil', was cremated on October 31 after his sudden death, which has left the
articles.body: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta, known for 'Kaante', 'Shootout at Lokhandwala' and 'Kaabil', was cremated on October 31 after his sudden death, which has left the film industry in shock. He reportedly died following a fall at his Versova residence. Colleagues and friends from the industry visited his home earlier in the day to pay their respects. Among them were Abhishek Bachchan, Manoj Bajpayee, Ronit Roy, Fardeen Khan, Farah Khan, Gulshan Grover, Milap Zaveri, Jaaved Jaaferi and Harshvardhan Rane. Rajpal Yadav said he was still struggling to accept the news.Rajpal Yadav reacts to Sanjay Gupta’s sudden deathRajpal struggled to find the right words while speaking to ANI, as colleagues from the film industry gathered to bid Gupta a final goodbye. His reaction mirrored the sorrow felt across Bollywood. Fighting back tears, Yadav said, “It is a tragic loss and difficult to understand. Everyone is incredibly sad. It is really unexpected, and there are simply no words for it. For someone to pass away at such a young age is just beyond words. May God grant peace to his soul and strength to his entire family. We could never imagine this kind of news.”How Sanjay Gupta was found dead at his Mumbai homeSanjay was discovered dead at his Mumbai home, reportedly after a fall late on the night of Friday, October 30. Police have filed an accidental death report and are looking into how it happened. According to the police, he sustained a serious head injury. The matter was reported the following morning, and he was subsequently declared dead. DCP North Zone-1 Purushottam Karad confirmed that Versova Police Station was informed about the filmmaker’s death and had logged an accidental death case.Sanjay Gupta’s family raises no suspicion, say policeAccording to police, the family raised no suspicions and did not lodge any complaint regarding how the incident occurred. A post-mortem examination has been started, and the investigation into the case is ongoing.Sanjay Gupta’s journey as a directorGupta began his career as a director with 'Aatish: Feel the Fire' in 1994. Over the years, he helmed several other films, including 'Kaante', 'Musafir', 'Zinda', 'Shootout at Wadala', 'Jazbaa' and 'Mumbai Saga'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'People are actually paying for it': Ritika Singh exposes fake Facebook account using her name; warns fans against Rs 400 subscription
articles.summary: Actor Ritika Singh has cautioned her followers against a Facebook page allegedly operating under her name and collecting money through paid subscriptions.
articles.body: Actor Ritika Singh has cautioned her followers against a Facebook page allegedly operating under her name and collecting money through paid subscriptions. The account reportedly charges users Rs 400 every month, despite having no official association with the actress. Ritika Singh addressed the issue through an Instagram video, explaining how people could mistake the page for an authentic account.She clarified that her verified Instagram profile is her only official social media account. The actress also raised concerns about AI-generated deepfake videos circulating in her name.Ritika Singh identifies fake Facebook page charging Rs 400Ritika Singh said she recently discovered a Facebook page using her identity to attract subscribers. According to the actress, the account operates through a monthly payment model and has already attracted people willing to pay for its content.She pointed out that the page does not carry a verification badge. Its creators have also misspelled her name, which she believes should alert users to its questionable authenticity. The actress urged people to check account details before making payments or subscribing to profiles claiming to represent celebrities.Actress clarifies which social media account is officialIn her Instagram video, Ritika Singh directly addressed the confusion surrounding the impersonating page. She emphasized that her verified profile is the only account she personally uses to share updates and content.“I am sharing this video to make it clear that the profile you are currently seeing is my only official account. This is my only verified account with a blue tick. Everything posted here is shared by me. However, I recently came across another page on Facebook that has been created in my name. They are running it on a subscription model, charging Rs 400 a month. People are actually paying for it. The page is not verified, and they have not even spelt my name correctly. Those who are paying for it should be a little more careful with their money,” she said in her Instagram video.Ritika Singh asks followers to report suspicious pageThe actress explained that she decided to speak publicly because she did not want her followers to continue believing the Facebook page was genuine. She also deliberately avoided sharing its link. According to her, promoting the account further could draw more attention to the people operating it.Instead, Ritika Singh asked users to exercise caution whenever they encounter profiles claiming to represent her. She also requested followers to report the suspicious Facebook page. The appeal was aimed at helping prevent further confusion and potentially getting the account taken down.Coming to her work front, Ritika Singh first gained recognition through her performance in the Tamil film 'Irudhi Suttru'. She subsequently appeared in projects across Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam cinema. Her most recent project in Malayalam is Dulquer Salmaan's 'King of Kotha'. articles.title: Telangana labour department issues notice to Ravi Teja starrer ‘Irumudi’ makers over child actor Nakshathra’s working conditions
articles.summary: The makers of Ravi Teja starrer ‘Irumudi’ have received a notice from the Telangana labour department over a complaint concerning child actor Baby
articles.body: The makers of Ravi Teja starrer ‘Irumudi’ have received a notice from the Telangana labour department over a complaint concerning child actor Baby Nakshathra’s participation in the film’s shooting and promotional activities. According to the updates, the makers are now set to meet the department next week.According to Telangana Today, a meeting with the production house, Mythri Movie Makers, has been scheduled for November 4 at Anjaiah Karmika Samkshema Bhavan in RTC X Roads.Complaint raises questions about working conditionsThe complaint was reportedly filed by C Mahesh Babu, founder-president of Jai Lok Satta (Social Justice Forum). It raises concerns about Nakshathra’s working hours, remuneration and other aspects of her participation in the film.The joint commissioner of labour for the Ranga Reddy Zone has summoned the production house to attend the meeting with the relevant records.The department is also expected to examine whether the conversations and language used during a promotional event affected the child actor’s dignity and safety.Producers asked to submit documentsThe labour department has reportedly sought documents relating to permission from the District Magistrate, parental consent, attendance, working hours, educational arrangements and safety measures for Nakshathra. The producers have also been asked to submit records of the child actor’s participation in promotional activities and details of whether 20% of her remuneration was deposited in a fixed deposit account in her name.About ‘Irumudi’In ‘Irumudi’, Ravi Teja plays Trinadh, an alcoholic father who decides to undertake Ayyappa Deeksha for his daughter, Manikanta, played by Baby Nakshathra. As part of the Deeksha, he must give up his vices and remain non-violent. However, he faces a difficult situation when he has to protect the girls in his village.The film also features Priya Bhavani Shankar, Sai Kumar, Sunil, Ramesh Indira and Swasika Vijay. GV Prakash Kumar has composed the music.Upon its release, ‘Irumudi’ turned out to be a huge hit as it collected Rs 224.42 crore in India gross and worldwide gross to Rs 246.87 crore as per trade analyst Sacnilk.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Actors Anish and Anaswara Rajan are gearing up for the Telugu romantic entertainer ‘Itlu Arjuna’ directed by Mahesh Uppala.
articles.body: Actors Anish and Anaswara Rajan are gearing up for the Telugu romantic entertainer ‘Itlu Arjuna’ directed by Mahesh Uppala. He also praised the young team’s passion and expressed confidence in the film’s love story.The film will now arrive in theatres on November 13, 2026.Nagarjuna wrote, “Watch out for #ItlluArjuna..!! The film’s romantic storyline and the chemistry between the lead pair have drawn attention ahead of its release. However, the makers have yet to reveal the complete story or officially confirm all the character details.Makers previously announced the delayWhen the film’s original release was postponed, the makers shared a message explaining the decision and asking audiences to continue supporting the team.They wrote, “We regret to inform that #ItlluArjuna will not be arriving on October 30th as planned. articles.title: 'Ramayana' actor Saurabh Sachdeva says online criticism doesn't bother him; calls film well-made; says religious sentiments make reactions sensitive
articles.summary: Actor Saurabh Sachdeva says he is not bothered by the online chatter and public scrutiny surrounding the much-anticipated film, \"Ramayana\", as the makers
articles.body: Actor Saurabh Sachdeva says he is not bothered by the online chatter and public scrutiny surrounding the much-anticipated film, "Ramayana", as the makers made it with a lot of care and authenticity.The film, billed as an ambitious global-scale adaptation of the Indian epic, features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita and Yash as Ravana. It is directed by Nitesh Tiwari of "Dangal" fame.After the release of the trailer, the film has received criticism over the visual effects and casting choices, including Kapoor's portrayal of Lord Ram.Sachdeva, known for featuring in films such as "Animal", "Eko" and "Pushpa 2: The Rule", among others, said the team knew religious subjects could evoke stronger reactions from people."It doesn't affect me. Now, people have a forum or place to talk about, they can say anything. If you are not getting the story and emotion right, then you can talk about not liking the film."Here (with 'Ramayana') definitely our belief is also connected, religious belief, religious sentiment is there, that is what is a little fragile. Hence, many times people will get up strongly and talk," Sachdeva told PTI in an interview.The actor said he "isn't scared". "I think the film is well-made, nothing has been added just to add, or we've not done anything just for the sake of it. Whatever I've seen, while dubbing for the film, I feel it is done in a beautiful and right way," he said.Sachdeva essays the role of the complex character Maricha in the mythological epic."I don't know how much of a villain Maricha is. He is on the villain side, but he is always in a dilemma about where to stand," he said.The actor lauded the film's director Tiwari, whom he described as a "calm and soft-spoken man"."He doesn't get agitated or upset. I haven't seen him screaming at anyone, he is a very relaxed person. He often says, 'You can do this, you can do that'."So, his calmness is very contagious, if the director is relaxed, then I'm also relaxed, and I don't have to be worried about it. I don't have to do anything."When asked about his expectations from part one of "Ramyana" on his career, Sachdeva said he hopes the film brings him more work."I hope I'll get a few more years (to work in the industry), more films, and that people will come to me. I think I will be known to Hollywood people also," he said."I feel that it will be a big hit, people will get to know more about me, more masses, and I'll get more films to do, and I'll entertain more fans," he added.Actors Arun Govil, Kunal Kapoor, Rakul Preet Singh, Lara Dutt, and Ravie Dubey round out the cast of the film.The first instalment of "Ramayana" is scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on November 5, 2026, while the second part is expected to arrive during Diwali 2027.The film will be released in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam languages.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Guys, please respect Dilip and my privacy': Farah Khan REACTS to viral video of argument with cook Dilip
articles.summary: Farah Khan has spoken out after a video showing an apparently heated exchange between her and her longtime cook, Dilip, circulated on social media.
articles.body: Farah Khan has spoken out after a video showing an apparently heated exchange between her and her longtime cook, Dilip, circulated on social media. The footage triggered discussions among viewers, with several people questioning what had happened between the two. Responding to the speculation, the filmmaker asked people to respect their privacy and avoid reaching conclusions based on a short clip.Farah Khan responds to speculationFarah Khan addressed the discussion through an Instagram post. She made it clear that people should not draw conclusions about her relationship with Dilip based on the circulating footage. The filmmaker also requested that viewers respect their personal space."Guys, please respect Dilip and my privacy. Do not jump to any conclusion (folded hands)," she wrote.Her response came after the video gained traction online. The clip shows Farah Khan and Dilip exchanging words in what appears to be a tense conversation. However, the footage does not establish what led to the disagreement.What happens in the viral video?In the video, Dilip is heard telling Farah Khan, "Maine kitni baar aapko bola hai." She responds, "Tu mujhe samjhayega?" The exchange has drawn attention because viewers are more accustomed to seeing the two share light-hearted moments in the kitchen.Farah Khan also appears to notice that someone is recording their conversation. She then asks the person behind the camera to stop filming. The brief footage has since prompted speculation about the circumstances surrounding their interaction.Neither the circulating clip nor the filmmaker's Instagram message provides further details about what happened before the exchange. Farah Khan's request, meanwhile, specifically asks viewers not to arrive at conclusions without knowing the full context.Dilip becomes a familiar face through Farah's vlogDilip is no longer just a behind-the-scenes member of Farah Khan's household. His appearances in her YouTube cooking videos have made him a recognizable personality among regular viewers. Their conversations often feature playful disagreements, sarcastic remarks and spontaneous humour.His straightforward personality and witty responses have become an important part of the videos.Farah Khan launched her cooking series on YouTube in 2024. The format brings together food preparation, celebrity appearances and conversations inside her kitchen. Rather than focusing exclusively on recipes, the videos also give viewers a glimpse of her interactions with guests.Their on-screen camaraderie draws attentionThe filmmaker's easy rapport with Dilip has remained one of the recurring attractions of her cooking videos. Their banter often provides some of the most entertaining moments, with Dilip's dry humour complementing Farah Khan's playful approach.On the work front, Farah Khan's last directorial was 'Happy New Year'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Hrithik Roshan wishes Saba Azad on her 40th birthday with heartfelt 'layover' note: 'I’d pick the 2nd option every time'
articles.summary: Hrithik Roshan and Saba Azad have been together for five years, and the pair is never shy about expressing their affection in public.
articles.body: Hrithik Roshan and Saba Azad have been together for five years, and the pair is never shy about expressing their affection in public. Having marked their fifth anniversary on October 1, Hrithik has now shared another special post for Saba. The actor wrote a sweet, heartfelt note for his girlfriend on social media as she turned 40 on November 1. In his Instagram post, Hrithik said that with her, every departure from the “normal inevitability” turns into a dance adventure.Hrithik Roshan’s flight analogy for Saba AzadSharing a post on Instagram, Hrithik wrote, “Someone asked me about you. I said I don’t wanna talk about you cause it’s too precious. She insisted and I said this .. “Well, how about this? Say if there were 2 options for flights from mumbai to a far off destination , one was a direct flight. Efficient and easy!”.Hrithik Roshan looks forward to a ‘lifetime of long layovers’The actor then described the second option: a flight out of Mumbai that stops in eight random cities, with hours of waiting at each one and a risk of missing the connection every time. “If it was with her... I said, I’d pick the 2nd option... deliberately... every single time,” he added. Concluding his note, Hrithik said he looks forward to a ‘lifetime fo long layovers’ with his girlfriend. “I love you. Happy Birthday,” he mentioned.His post begins with a close-up of Saba, and the second slide has a funny video of her. In the third, the couple share a playful boomerang, and the following three slides show the actress looking happy. The seventh and eighth slides are cheerful, candid moments of the two together. The last slide features Saba smiling alongside Hrithik’s sons, Hrehaan Roshan and Hridaan Roshan, from his first marriage to Sussanne Khan.Hrithik Roshan’s work frontOn the work front, Hrithik was last seen in a special appearance in Rajinikanth’s 'Jailer 2', directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, which was a big success at the box office. Prior to that, he had a cameo in 'Alpha', starring Alia Bhatt, Sharvari and Bobby Deol. Before both of these, he appeared in 'War 2' alongside Jr NTR and Kiara Advani. articles.summary: Actress Juhi Chawla wished fellow actress Aishwarya Rai Bachchan on her birthday with a heartfelt post.
articles.body: Actress Juhi Chawla wished fellow actress Aishwarya Rai Bachchan on her birthday with a heartfelt post.Juhi praised Aishwarya for her beauty and grace in a special post that read, "Happy Birthday Aishwarya! So much grace, beauty and poise... and somehow always making it all look effortless ..!! Wishing you a wonderful year ahead, with lots of happiness and many many beautiful moments. (sic)."It must be noted that Juhi and Aishwarya have never had a chance to share screen space in a project.Meanwhile, the netizens remain excited for any update on the life of the former beauty queen.On October 24, Aishwarya was seen celebrating her nephew Shivansh Rai's birthday. The 'Devdas' actress was accompanied by her daughter Aaradhya Bachchan and the other members of the Rai family during the celebration.Aishwarya's sister-in-law, Shrima Rai, treated the netizens to a couple of glimpses of the intimate celebration on her official handle.The photographs from the birthday celebration showed Aishwarya, Aaradhya, Shrima, Aishwarya's brother Aditya Rai, and Aishwarya's mother Vrinda Rai. The happy pic had the family gathering around the birthday boy. We could also see a cake and a bouquet of flowers placed on the table.Sharing the pictures, Shrima wrote the caption, "Happy Birthday to my cutie pie @shivansh_rai23. Here's to more pranks, more time with nature, more laughter and blessings. articles.title: 'La 1' supera a 'Antena 3' y se convierte en la televisión líder de España: la más vista de un mes de octubre desde 2011
articles.standfirst: El presidente de RTVE ha celebrado en redes sociales este hito con un mensaje claro: "No era imposible"
articles.summary: El presidente de RTVE ha celebrado en redes sociales este hito con un mensaje claro: "No era imposible"
articles.body: 'La 1' de Televisión Española (TVE) ha protagonizado uno de los cambios más destacables del panorama televisivo reciente al coronarse como la cadena más vista de España durante el pasado mes de octubre de 2026. Con un crecimiento de un punto respecto al periodo anterior, el canal público ha alcanzado un destacado 13% de cuota de pantalla, un registro que no lograba dominar en este mes específico desde el año 2011. Este éxito no se debe a un único acierto aislado, sino a una estrategia transversal consolidada en todas las franjas horarias. 'La 1' se ha erigido como líder indiscutible de la mañana con un 18,8%, de la tarde alcanzando el 10,8% y, de manera muy significativa, del codiciado prime time con un 13%, demostrando una sólida fidelización de la audiencia a lo largo de toda la jornada. Por su parte, 'Antena 3' ha cerrado el mes de octubre con un 12,5% de cuota de pantalla media siendo la primera entre las televisiones privadas aunque por detrás de la cadena pública. Eso sí, Antena 3 Noticias continúa siendo uno de sus mayores pilares y el informativo más visto de la televisión con un 24% de cuota de pantalla. 'Telecinco' sufre aunque se mantiene terera con un 8,5%, seguida de 'Cuatro' con un 7,5%, 'La Sexta' con un 5,5% y 'La 2' con un 3,3% de cuota de pantalla. Desde RTVE han celebrado la noticia con entusiasmo, una alegría que ha sido personificada en José Pablo López, presidente de la corporación, y que ha recordado que este hito histórico demuestra que el objetivo nunca fue una quimera: "No era imposible. Somos la primera cadena del país". El tirón de la programación ha sabido conectar con una amplia y diversa masa de espectadores, desbancando a sus principales competidores privados y reconfigurando el mapa de preferencias de la audiencia española. Este liderazgo refuerza el papel del ente público en un entorno de máxima competencia. La dirección y los rostros visibles de la cadena han querido trasladar un mensaje de profundo reconocimiento hacia los espectadores que han confiado en sus contenidos. Con un escueto pero sincero "Gracias", la cadena cierra un mes dorado que marca un punto de inflexión en su trayectoria reciente.

The space once belonged to none other than Elvis Presley and was bought by him and his wife, Priscilla Presley, in 1967 for roughly USD 400,000 shortly after their wedding. This is where the couple resided for most of their time, specifically around the time of when Presley was at the height of his career. Now, according to a recent report, the estate has been made available for rent since earlier this year.Elvis Presley and Priscilla Presley bought the home in 1967Designed in 1958 by Master Architect Rex Lotery, the 5,300-square-foot residence blends mid-century modern design such as large windows, an open layout, skylights, and coffered ceilings with Hollywood Regency entrance details. Set on a 1.18-acre promontory offering panoramic views of the Los Angeles skyline and the Pacific Ocean. The home features 4 bedrooms, 5 bathrooms, sliding glass doors throughout, a pool, a hot tub, a patio, and sprawling lawns.Another key feature of the property is the wall-to-wall glass sliding doors, which allow unbroken views of the surrounding city skyline and ocean from inside. articles.title: Quote of the day by Pedro Pascal: "I always say rejection is redirection, rejection is protection. And it worked out in the end," a gentle nudge to trust the process and keep going
articles.summary: Actor Pedro Pascal shares a powerful message about rejection and opportunity, encouraging us to trust the process of life. His journey highlights how setbacks can lead to unexpected success and reminds us that everyone experiences disappointments on their path to success.
articles.body: Not every opportunity we lose is a setback. Sometimes a job rejection, a failed audition or a plan that falls through nudges us towards something we hadn’t even considered. Disappointment is hard to sit with in the moment, but looking back, you can sometimes see that a different path was waiting all along. Actor Pedro Pascal shared a thought that captures this feeling really well.Today’s quote of the day by Pedro Pascal reads: “I always say rejection is redirection, rejection is protection. And it worked out in the end.”What does Pedro Pascal’s quote mean?Pascal said this in a May 2024 interview with GQ, while talking about an audition he did for the HBO series ‘Looking’ in early 2013. He didn’t get the part, but the experience eventually pointed him towards other opportunities. Pedro Pascal's next big break came when he landed a role in Narcos, and that ended up being a real turning point for his career.Pedro's story is basically a reminder to cut yourself some slack when things don't go to plan. Rejection has a way of knocking your confidence, and it's super easy to start feeling like everyone else is zooming ahead while you're stuck in the same place. But one letdown doesn't mean your chances are gone. Sometimes life just takes a detour, and there's still loads of room for good stuff to turn up.Imagine someone who puts everything into landing their dream job and doesn't get it. Ouch, right? Especially after weeks of prepping and crossing fingers. But that sting can also be the push they needed to level up their skills, try a different route, or stumble into a place where they actually feel at home.Why does Pedro Pascal's message still matter today?People love sharing their wins, promotions and happy moments, but they rarely talk about the disappointments that came first. That can make it seem like everyone else is moving ahead while you’re still trying to find your way.Pascal's story is a good reminder that everybody gets there in their own time. Maybe you didn't get into the college you were dreaming of. Maybe you bombed a few auditions in a row, or got passed over for that promotion you were so sure about. It stings when things don't go the way you pictured, no doubt about it.His words also nudge us to separate our self-worth from other people’s decisions. Not getting picked doesn’t automatically mean you lack talent or potential. Sometimes the timing, the requirements or the circumstances just don’t line up.Pedro Pascal’s early lifeJose Pedro Balmaceda Pascal was born on April 2, 1975, in Santiago, Chile. His family left the country when he was an infant because of the political situation under the military dictatorship of Augusto Pinochet. They eventually settled in the United States, and Pascal grew up in Texas and California.He got interested in acting at a young age and studied at the Orange County School of the Arts. He later went to New York University’s Tisch School of the Arts, where he trained in drama.It wasn’t an overnight success story. Before he became a familiar face on television, Pascal spent years going to auditions, performing in theatre and taking smaller roles.How did Pedro Pascal rise to fame?Pedro Pascal's career didn't start with a big splash. He spent years picking up small TV roles, popping up in shows like Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Law & Order, and doing theatre on the side. He just kept showing up and taking whatever came his way, slowly carving out a spot for himself. For a long time, though, hardly anyone really noticed him.That finally changed in 2014, when he turned up as Oberyn Martell in season four of Game of Thrones. Viewers latched onto the character almost immediately, and it gave Pascal the breakthrough he'd been chasing for ages. People couldn't stop talking about his performance, and suddenly he had fans all over the world.He went on to play DEA agent Javier Pena in ‘Narcos’ and later became hugely popular as the title character in ‘The Mandalorian’. His turn as Joel in the drama series ‘The Last of Us’ strengthened his standing even further and earned him major award nominations.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Congress can save America’s unique history and boost the economy with just one move
articles.summary: Trump urged Congress to pass a federal film tax credit as the U.S. share of global production has dropped from 65% to 39%, threatening American jobs.
articles.body: One of us represents historic American studios that develop and distribute the world’s greatest films and TV shows. Another represents 1.3 million hardworking Americans, including tens of thousands of drivers, transportation professionals, casting directors, animal wranglers and location scouts who are vital to the entertainment industry. And the third represents nearly 170,000 highly skilled behind-the-scenes workers who bring these stories to life. At times we’re on opposite sides of the table, but we share a north star: to grow and maintain a thriving American film and television business that creates good jobs and boosts local communities nationwide. We stand together today urging Congress to pass a long-overdue federal film incentive this year and to join us in protecting American jobs that keep our nation at the forefront of visual storytelling. The film and TV industry has always been an American economic engine, generating over 2 million jobs nationwide every year. These production jobs impact and support more than 162,000 businesses across all 50 states. The industry pays over $200 billion in wages to U.S. workers each year and holds a trade surplus with nearly every nation on Earth. HOLLYWOOD STAR SOUNDS ALARM OVER DISAPPEARING JOBS AS PRODUCTIONS FLEE CALIFORNIA When a national poll asked Americans what the U.S. does better than anyone else in the world, the top answer wasn't tech or finance, music or sports. It was movies and TV. Work in this space is a national occupation, taking advantage of unbeatable locations — from Montana’s big skies to Hawaii’s blue waters. In recent years, many states have established highly effective tax incentive programs to make local shooting even more competitive. It’s easy to see why: an average feature film adds $22 million to the economy where it shoots and a TV series production can be expected to hire 1,800 workers a season. PELOSI, OMAR JOIN TRUMP AND SCHIFF AS UNLIKELY ALLIANCE PUSHES TO ONSHORE KEY INDUSTRY Congress must build on this success by enacting a federal tax incentive that will boost production and lift up workers in every state. Republicans and Democrats collectively recognize that other nations have long been taking advantage of similar tax incentives to attract these projects and jobs. As a result of more than 120 jurisdictions around the world offering production incentives, the U.S. share of global production has slipped from a historic 65% benchmark to just 39% today. This significant decline isn’t an abstract statistic — it translates into dark soundstages, unreliable paychecks and fewer good-paying American jobs from coast to coast. PARAMOUNT ESCALATES THREAT TO LEAVE CALIFORNIA AS DEM AG'S ANTITRUST LAWSUIT STALLS WARNER BROS MERGER A federal film tax incentive will ensure America reclaims its production leadership by making domestic shoots cost-competitive. And the results will be profound. A new study found that returning the U.S. to its historic 65% share of global production would add almost $250 billion to local economies and create more than 143,000 additional jobs per year. A separate look at film and TV production decision-making found that this type of program would make 80% of the projects competitive to shoot here at home. FILM PRODUCER SAYS 'MADE IN AMERICA' MOVIES CAN HELP REVIVE HOLLYWOOD'S STRUGGLING INDUSTRY States that have had programs in place for years prove tax incentives quickly pay for themselves. One study found that the Georgia film tax credit delivers a 6.3-to-1 "return on investment" by generating new economic activity. Another determined Texas adds $4.50 to the local economy for every dollar invested in the state’s incentive. The federal government already backs strategically important industries with similarly targeted incentives to keep American jobs in America, from pharma to aerospace and automobiles. The film and television industry should be no different. Research shows that after watching American-made movies and shows, foreign audiences are significantly more likely to want to visit the U.S., buy American products and engage with American culture and history. This tangible global impact benefits each of us every day. Congress must build on this success by enacting a federal tax incentive that will boost production and lift up workers in every state. We are grateful for President Donald Trump’s leadership on prioritizing and protecting American jobs in this industry. This urgent effort was boosted by the president’s recent call for Congress to "approve, immediately, a Federal Production Incentive to create Entertainment Jobs in America." CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION We strongly support the president’s call and commend the bipartisan coalition of congressional allies for introducing the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act in the U.S. Senate and House, including Sens. Tim Scott, R-S.C., and Adam Schiff, D-Calif., as well as Reps. Nathaniel Moran, R-Texas, Linda Sánchez, D-Calif., Brian Jack, R-Ga., and Laura Friedman, D-Calif., along with the more than 50 bipartisan sponsors. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP America has long led the world in film and television production. For more than a century, it has been inherently woven into our shared American identity. We must never sacrifice our leadership, innovation or pride of ownership. There are countless more stories to tell, and we remain confident that this industry’s brightest days are yet to be imagined. But Congress must first do its job to ensure every American impacted by this essential industry can get back to work.

articles.title: Why everybody still loves 'Raymond' 30 years later: How suburban family chaos became comedy gold
articles.summary: As "Everybody Loves Raymond" marks 30 years, stars and creators reveal the real marital battles, backstage rules and lucky breaks behind the timeless classic.
articles.body: When "Everybody Loves Raymond" debuted 30 years ago, it showed how a stand-up comic from Queens and a series about suburban in-laws could thrive on primetime network television. Three decades, nine seasons and 69 Emmy nominations later, the classic sitcom has stood the test of time and remains a comfort show for generations of viewers. Now, as star Ray Romano and his longtime manager, Rory Rosegarten — an executive producer on the show — prepare for induction into the Long Island Music and Entertainment Hall of Fame, the show's stars and creative team are reflecting on the real-life experiences that helped make it a lasting success. ‘FAMILY AFFAIR’ STAR KATHY GARVER SAYS FAILED REMAKE ‘SUCKED,’ REVEALS WHAT WENT WRONG Speaking with Fox News Digital, Patricia Heaton said "Everybody Loves Raymond" reflected her own experiences with marriage and motherhood, making it more than just another Hollywood sitcom pilot. "It wasn’t an overnight success; it was a humble family comedy that, over the years, has resonated worldwide," Heaton said. "It wasn’t flashy, just incredibly funny and relatable. I found it mirrored my own personal life with my marriage and kids, which is how you know it was going to be relatable to a huge audience." Heaton said the cast, including Romano, Brad Garrett, Doris Roberts, Peter Boyle, was "perfectly suited to their characters" and that each year the scripts got "funnier and funnier." She recalled table reads as some of her favorite days of the week. "All those episodes continue to reflect the joys and struggles of families all around the world, from generation to generation," Heaton said. "It was a joy to perform, a joy to watch, and a joy to know that we brought a little bit of happiness to people’s lives." KELSEY GRAMMER ADMITS SURPRISING REASON 'FRASIER' ALMOST NEVER HAPPENED But before the Barone family became a television favorite, the series hinged on a stand-up comic and the manager who discovered him at a New York radio station's comedy competition. Rosegarten, Romano's longtime manager, first encountered the comedian while judging the competition. He was immediately drawn to Romano's grounded, self-deprecating routine about his wife and kids. "When I saw Ray that first time, it was love at first sight," Rosegarten told Fox News Digital. "He was so original, and he was talking about real life, not made-up stuff. Not a piece of hair on a soap, but he was talking about his wife and his kids and his life. I wish I could tell you I knew what would happen to him, would happen. I don’t think anybody could predict that. But I thought he was really funny." Rosegarten said he later used his connections to secure Romano an appearance on the "Late Show with David Letterman." LORNE MICHAELS’ ‘SNL’ GRIP ON CAST EXPOSED IN NEW DOCUMENTARY "He went on the show, and he killed," Rosegarten recalled. "He killed in such a way that to this day I still use that footage to show people exactly how to do it. Like, that should be the guideline." That appearance helped pave the way for a CBS pilot, though Rosegarten said getting the family sitcom on network television also came down to luck. "We shot a pilot for CBS, and Les Moonves, who then was the president of CBS, literally took the tape home over the weekend," Rosegarten said. "It’s pilot season, and I’m sure he had a million shows to watch. But he watched that one with his family and they liked it." "I lay in bed sometimes, and I think if he had been late that night for a dinner, or he had been fighting with someone in the office, and he didn't take the tape, I might not be talking to you right now," he added. "So there's a little luck involved, too." 'HOME IMPROVEMENT' STAR SAYS PATRICIA RICHARDSON GOT 'TIRED' OF FIGHTING FOR SITCOM "Everybody Loves Raymond" premiered Sept. 13, 1996, and ran for nine seasons before its finale in 2005. The sitcom won 15 Emmy Awards and followed Italian American sportswriter Ray Barone as he navigated marriage, fatherhood and the interference of his parents and brother, who lived across the street on Long Island. Rosegarten credited much of the show's success to its writing, which drew heavily from the real-life experiences of the writing staff and cast. He recalled a rule established by creator and showrunner Phil Rosenthal that discouraged late nights in the writers' room. "We were one of the very few shows where everybody went home at six o’clock," Rosegarten said. "Because Phil’s attitude was: 'Go home, have a fight with your wife, we’ll talk about it tomorrow, and we’ll write about it.' And that was a stroke of genius, actually." That emphasis on everyday family life helped revitalize the traditional sitcom, according to Ron Simon, head curator at the Paley Center for Media. "The importance of 'Everybody Loves Raymond' is that it revitalized the family situation comedy," Simon told Fox News Digital. "It debuted in 1996 and it sort of brought a whole new life to one of the staples of television comedy from the very beginning. 'Everybody Loves Raymond' was able to take a look at all these different frustrations of suburban life in Long Island and really create a cast that anyone watching could identify with." Simon pointed to the show's familiar family dynamics as a key part of its appeal. "They took frustrations that happened in their own lives and then adapted them for the situation comedy, so it was very real," Simon said. "No matter who you were, whether it was domestic squabbles between Ray and Debra, the intrusiveness of the mother and father. And of course, there’s always sibling rivalry between Ray and Robert. So, it just had a great formula." The show's Long Island roots are now being recognized as Romano and Rosegarten prepare to enter the Long Island Music and Entertainment Hall of Fame. The pair is being honored as the institution's first non-music inductees. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Ray and I are very honored and very thrilled with the induction. And to be the first non-music inductees, I think it's unbelievable," Rosegarten said. "Kiss is in there, and Billy Joel and Clive Davis. It's weird. It's like a who's who. I look at Ray, and Ray looks at me like they must have made a mistake somewhere along the line."

articles.title: Shah Rukh Khan sneaks out for a late-night drive to see ‘King’ tribute on Mumbai’s Sea Link ahead of 61st birthday

articles.body: The excitement surrounding Shah Rukh Khan’s birthday is beginning to build across the country. With the Bollywood superstar set to turn 61 on Monday, November 2, fans, well-wishers and his team are gearing up to celebrate the occasion in a grand way. The celebrations come at a particularly exciting time for the actor, with less than nine weeks remaining for the worldwide release of his upcoming film, director Siddharth Anand’s ‘King’ (2026).Adding to the birthday buzz, Shah Rukh recently made a late-night visit to catch a special tribute dedicated to ‘King’ in Mumbai. The actor stepped out for a drive to see the massive film-themed display installed along the Bandra-Worli Sea Link. Sharing pictures of the installation on X (formerly Twitter), he thanked Google Gemini for the gesture, writing, “Dost ho toh Google Gemini jaisa (A friend should be like Google Gemini). Thank you for the KING-sized love always. I had to sneak out for a drive to get this photo, ha ha.”Meanwhile, speculation is rife that the makers of ‘King’ are planning to release a special teaser on Shah Rukh’s birthday. Videos and photographs of a massive screen being installed outside his residence, Mannat, have further fuelled the buzz, with fans wondering whether the teaser will be unveiled and screened there. However, reports suggest that the actor will once again not make his customary balcony appearance to greet fans, continuing a trend from the past two years.The film’s director, Siddharth Anand, has also been adding to the anticipation. Since Thursday, October 29, he has been posting cryptic phrases on X, one each day, which appear to be part of a larger sentence. The final post is expected on Monday. So far, his posts have read, “It’s time for the world to celebrate the King of…”The birthday celebrations are not limited to Mumbai, with fans travelling from different parts of the country to be near Mannat for the occasion. Shah Rukh’s fan association in Pune, Maharashtra, has also announced plans to organise what it describes as the biggest first-day-first-show (FDFS) celebration for ‘King’ in the city. Other chapters of the fan organisation are similarly stepping up promotional activities for the action thriller.Apart from Shah Rukh, ‘King’ features Suhana Khan, Abhishek Bachchan, Deepika Padukone, Anil Kapoor, Rani Mukerji and Jaideep Ahlawat in key roles. articles.body: Hollywood's much-loved couple Zendaya and Tom Holland are reportedly taking another big step in their life together by purchasing a lavish £9 million property in Wimbledon, southwest London. The couple, who tied the knot earlier this year after meeting on the sets of the Spider-Man franchise, have reportedly bought a sprawling home close to the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club, the venue for the prestigious Wimbledon Championships.According to a report by The Daily Mail, the property offers considerable privacy, expansive outdoor spaces and even a private tennis court. Set across nearly an acre of land, the house also comes with a separate cottage, making it a substantial addition to the couple's property portfolio.The nearly £9 million property reportedly features four reception rooms and has been described by estate agents as offering an 'outstanding blend of space, privacy and versatility'.Spread across almost an acre, the residence includes a large garden, a separate cottage and a private tennis court. Given Zendaya's association with tennis following her role in Challengers, the property's sporting facility makes for an interesting feature.The house is also located close to the All England Club, where Zendaya watched the 2024 Wimbledon finals. Tom, who grew up in Kingston upon Thames, around four miles from the property, has previously spoken about how special it was to see his wife in a place he considers home.Tom Holland once praised Zendaya's Wimbledon appearanceZendaya's connection with tennis became particularly prominent while she was promoting her 2024 film Challengers, in which she played a former tennis prodigy turned coach. During the film's promotional campaign, she made headlines for her fashion choices, including a custom-made Loewe dress paired with stiletto heels featuring yellow tennis balls.She later attended the 2024 Wimbledon finals at Centre Court, where she was spotted wearing a series of Ralph Lauren suits.Tom was particularly taken by her appearance and spoke about it during an interview with GQ. Recalling the occasion, he said, 'She just looked so beautiful and so at home. It meant so much for her to be in a place that I call home and look like such a part of our community.'The couple's reported decision to buy a property in Wimbledon now brings them closer to the area that holds personal significance for Tom.Zendaya and Tom Holland's new home could face a neighbourhood development battleWhile the property offers considerable privacy, its location could also place the couple close to a long-running local controversy.According to The Daily Mail, the house is adjacent to the historic Grade II-listed Wimbledon Park Golf Club, a golf course designed around a lake and dotted with oak trees planted by renowned landscape gardener Lancelot 'Capability' Brown.The All England Club has proposed developing the former golf course into a major tennis facility, featuring an 8,000-seat stadium and 38 additional courts. However, the plans have faced opposition from campaigning group Save Wimbledon Park, which argues that the land is protected by a statutory trust under a law dating back 150 years.The golf course was closed after its members sold the leasehold to the All England Club for £65 million. Its future remains subject to legal proceedings, with the matter awaiting a judgment from the Court of Appeal.It remains unclear whether the proposed development will affect the couple's new surroundings.Couple keeping a low profile at their new propertyDespite the reported purchase, Zendaya and Tom have not yet been spotted by local residents at the Wimbledon property. The neighbour added that they had joked about how far a football would need to travel to reach the couple's back garden, while suggesting that a housewarming party was unlikely.The actors are known for keeping their personal lives private. articles.title: Christopher Lloyd says he and Michael J. Fox didn’t become friends until after“ Back to the Future” films
articles.summary: The two had a chaotic introduction while shooting a scene for the first movie.
articles.body:
Christopher Lloyd shared that he and Michael J. Fox became friends after the Back to the Future films.

The two were "separated by a generation" and preoccupied with their work, especially during the first movie.

Lloyd wrote about stories from his days filming the Back to the Future trilogy in his memoir In My Own Time , out now.

Christopher Lloyd admitted that it took a while for his friendship with Michael J. Fox to bloom.

The 87-year-old reflected on his time working with Fox during the Back to the Future trilogy. Their introduction came under unusual and stressful circumstances, as the Family Ties alum had been brought in to replace Eric Stoltz as Marty McFly six weeks into shooting the first film.

"So as far as I can tell, our introduction happened in a parking lot on Back to the Future, as Doc Brown and Marty, at a time when we were re-shooting scenes that I had already done once before," Lloyd wrote in his memoir In My Own Time . "I was having a very self-involved reaction at first, and moment to moment I was feeling the challenge of it, knowing that I had to make Doc's scenes happen again and worrying about whether I could bring them back to the level I had brought them to the first time."

Needless to say, Lloyd was preoccupied with the retakes, so getting to know Fox wasn't the priority. Still, as the actors were "feeling each other out" during scenes, the Taxi alum said things "seemed to be clicking."

"I was extremely grateful that the other actor in this case was Michael, because he brought his own energy and that sparked me to get over my own anxieties," Lloyd continued.

But although they had great chemistry onscreen, the 88-year-old admitted that they largely kept to themselves during their downtime. He also noted that Fox had been keeping a hectic schedule, as he had been filming Back to the Future and Family Ties concurrently.

"We were separated by a generation in age, and he was busy doing essentially two jobs at once, one of which was a movie where everyone else had already done many more weeks' worth of work, and now he was expected to come in quickly and help save the day. It must have been a very heavy burden for him," Lloyd shared.

As a result, the two weren't very close. In fact, the One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest actor said that it took filming the rest of the trilogy to establish a friendship.

"It would take two more Back to the Future movies before Michael and I truly got to know each other and become friends. But it would come," Lloyd shared.

In his memoir, Lloyd recounted several standout moments during his time filming the Back to the Future movies. He revealed that his favorite installment was Back to the Future Part III, although he also shared that he had one regret while working on the movie.

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

While he was explicitly told not to do his own stunts, there was one in particular that Lloyd believed he could pull off. During the climactic scene where Doc and Marty ride up to a train on horseback in an attempt to make it back to 1985, Lloyd admitted that he wished he had hoisted himself onto the train himself, rather than let a stuntman do it for him.

"Who knows what would have happened next? But whenever I watch the movie and see that scene, I still feel that pang in my heart: I should have done it," he said.

In My Own Time is available now wherever books are sold.

articles.title: 'Heat' director Michael Mann accidentally shoots himself at L.A. gun range
articles.summary: The 83-year-old filmmaker suffered a minor injury when a gun discharged while holstered. His representative said he was treated at a hospital and is being re...
articles.body:
Michael Mann, the acclaimed filmmaker behind crime thrillers including "Heat" (1995) and "Collateral" (2004), accidentally shot himself in the leg Saturday at a Los Angeles gun range, suffering a minor injury.

"On Saturday, at a gun range, a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered, resulting in a superficial injury to film director Michael Mann," his representative said in a statement Sunday. "He was treated and is being released."

Mann, 83, was engaged in target practice at a sanctioned shooting range when the accident occurred. The director has been an experienced target shooter for decades, according to a person familiar with the circumstances, who described the injury as minor and subcutaneous.

The shooting occurred around 4 p.m. Saturday at the Range LA, according to TMZ , which first reported the incident. Police and paramedics responded, and Mann was taken by ambulance to a hospital.

Mann is known for his painstaking attention to detail and realistic depictions of gun violence, perhaps most famously in the elaborate bank robbery shootout in "Heat," in which Robert De Niro and Val Kilmer's heavily armed crew exchange gunfire with police on the streets of downtown Los Angeles. He is developing a sequel to the film, which is expected to begin shooting early next year.

Mann also helped define the look and feel of the influential 1980s television series "Miami Vice," serving as executive producer before directing a 2006 film adaptation. His other credits include "Thief" (1981), "The Last of the Mohicans" (1992), "The Insider" (1999), which earned seven Oscar nominations, "Ali" (2001) and "Ferrari" (2023).

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Heidi Klum, Queen of Halloween, reveals this year’s ‘bloody’ costume: A giant severed hand
articles.summary: Heidi Klum arrived at her 25th annual Halloween party as a giant, bloody severed hand, a replica of her own left hand, right down to her wedding ring.
articles.body:
Heidi Klum's "bloody" Halloween costume is finally here. The supermodel arrived at her 25th annual Halloween party in New York on Saturday as a giant, gruesome severed hand.

Only her eyes and mouth showed, with blood dripping from her mouth as she stuck out her tongue, the Associated Press reported . Her legs formed two of the fingers, and helpers in blood-stained hazmat suits walked her down the carpet at Cathédrale.

The hand is a replica of her own left one, with long red nails, a thumb ring, and her engagement ring and wedding band.

"I looked at my hand and I thought, 'Hey, I think I could fit my body in this somehow,'" Klum told the AP.

It took about five to six hours to get into the costume, she said, adding, "Hands down, the hardest thing is carrying it. It's quite heavy."

Longtime collaborator Mike Marino, a special effects makeup artist, used scans of her body to build it. "It's not just any giant hand: It's my giant hand!" Klum told Vogue, according to Vanity Fair .

Her husband, Tom Kaulitz, missed the party because he is on tour, but the costume includes the tattoo of his name on her ring finger. "A little bit of Tom is with me," she told the AP. She also joked to USA Today that he "could have been the other hand."

Klum spent the week before the party teasing the look on Instagram, including close-ups of prosthetics that resembled organs and tissue, and images of a misshapen mouth. She also told USA Today that her body would "fit in a shape that normally a human body would not fit in." Fans guessed everything from Monstro Elisasue from The Substance to a Clicker from The Last of Us.

Before the party, Marino told NBC's Hollywood ReelTime that this year's look was "one of the most elaborate costumes ever made."

"It's so difficult to do and just the complication of it is really challenging," Marino said. "It might not appear to some people sometimes how much work goes into it but there's so much that goes into these things."

Klum first teased the costume on Oct. 24, sharing a close-up on Instagram of prosthetics resembling human organs. Fans were quick to guess, with answers ranging from "Coral reef. Inspired by St. Barth's" to "pirates of the caribbean when the pirates become sea creatures on the flying dutchman."

"Internal organs?" one commenter asked, while another remarked, "Looks like the inside of a stomach."

"Idk but I'm gagging already," admitted another fan.

When it comes to her costume for All Hallows' Eve, Klum has a history of going all-out . Over the years, Klum has consistently debuted high-concept, unsightly transformations. Her greatest hits include E.T., a gigantic peacock, a slinky worm, a skin-baring zombie creature and Fiona from Shrek . Last year, Klum slithered into her costume bash as Medusa, complete with a scaled body, a tail and a head of snakes. In past years, Kaulitz has joined in, dressing as the Greek soldier that Medusa turned to stone, a bloodied fisherman and the Shrek to her Fiona.

Klum opened up about what sparked her desire to throw a costume party every Halloween, telling Parade, "I'd go to some of these Halloween parties and people were just not given anything."

Klum isn't concerned with looking sexy on Halloween. In fact, she prefers to go in the complete opposite direction. After seeing one too many unimpressive costumes, she decided to take matters into her own hands, hosting her first Halloween party in 2000.

"This is really how it sparked my idea on doing one myself because I thought all the parties were so lame and the costumes people were doing even lamer," Klum told Parade. "I was like, 'There needs to be a person who really shows them to give more.'"

articles.title: Heidi Klum’s severed hand, Harry Styles’ Pizza Rat and more: The best celebrity Halloween costumes of 2026
articles.summary: Heidi Klum’s giant severed hand, Harry Styles as Pizza Rat and Kim Kardashian as North West are among the best celebrity Halloween costumes of 2026.
articles.body:
Is it really Halloween if celebrities don't go all out with their costumes? The spookiest night of the year has come and gone, and everyone from actors and artists to athletes and public figures showed off their looks. Whether it's an obscure, avant-garde take on a larger concept or a faithful — and playful — transformation into a fellow celebrity, the stars have a knack for dressing up.

Below, Yahoo has rounded up the best Halloween costumes of 2026.

The Queen of Halloween went gory for her 25th annual party in New York, arriving as a giant, bloody severed hand . The costume is a replica of her own left hand, complete with red nails, her wedding band and the tattoo of husband Tom Kaulitz's name. "Hands down, the hardest thing is carrying it," she told the Associated Press.

Harry Styles went all the way back to the beginning. At the first of his two "Harryween" shows at Madison Square Garden on Friday, the singer, 32, recreated his 2010 X Factor audition , right down to the grey cardigan, yellow scarf and pinned-on audition number . He sang Stevie Wonder's "Isn't She Lovely" and told the crowd, "I work in a bakery." Earlier in the night, he dressed as Elvis Presley, in a white sequined jumpsuit and cape, with Presley's granddaughter Riley Keough in the crowd.

For the final night of his 30-night residency on Saturday, he dressed as New York's "Pizza Rat," in a furry brown suit with a long pink tail and a giant slice of foam pizza. Zoë Kravitz went as a bodega plastic bag .

Paris Hilton continued her tradition of dressing up as Britney Spears , this time recreating the pop star's look in the "I'm a Slave 4 U" music video. Hilton also included her family in this year's costumes. The Simple Life star, her husband Carter Reum and their two children brought characters from Beauty and the Beast to life. Reum was the Beast, son Phoenix was Lumiere, daughter London was Chip and Hilton was Belle — a decision that garnered backlash online . Those weren't their only costumes, though: Hilton also dressed up as goth matriarch Morticia Addams, while her hubby and kiddos rounded out the Addams family.

Ticketmaster… but make it wearable? Lily Allen dressed up as the ticketing platform's infamous seating map, wearing a matching white puffer and leotard covered with little blue dots. (We can't get over the "Stage" detail across the collar.) Allen shared her costume on Instagram with the caption, "Never beating the allegations. #bluedotfever." One fan explained the West End Girl singer's costume in the comments.

"For anyone who is missing the joke - Lily canceled her Auckland concert due to being sick," she wrote. "People online said it was because she didn't sell enough tickets. Geddit now? 🫩"

During Friday's broadcast, the Today show hosts debuted their transformations for this year's festivities. Standout costumes included Savannah Guthrie as an old-school news anchor, Al Roker as Gumby and Jenna Bush Hager as Phoebe Buffay from Friends . Our personal favorite? Carson Daly, who dressed up as "Choosin' Texas" hitmaker Ella Langley. Daly hilariously brought the country darling to life — complete with her signature fringe.

Kim Kardashian doesn't play when it comes to Halloween. This year, the Skims founder dressed up as someone near and dear to her heart: her daughter North West! From her long, electric-blue hair and piercings to her signature hand-covering-mouth pose, Kardashian was the spitting image of North.

Keke Palmer and her son, Leodis, channeled 1995-era Janet Jackson and Michael Jackson from their acclaimed "Scream" music video. Palmer transformed into the "All for You" singer, while 3-year-old Leodis made an adorable King of Pop.

"Another memory with mommy and son! I LOVE YOU SO MUCH BUDDY. ITS SO MUCH FUN PLAYING WITH YOU! You will take over the family business, your way, someday," Palmer wrote on Instagram. "My SCREAM come true. 🥹🖤"

They're going stateside! Overcompensating stars Owen Thiele and Benito Skinner dressed up as PinkPantheress and Zara Larsson from their "Stateside" music video. articles.title: The Hollywood Hills home of Dorothy Dandridge, the first Black woman nominated for the best actress Oscar, has four bedrooms, stained-glass windows and skyline views; it last sold for $2.9 million in 2014 and is now listed for $5.5 million
articles.summary: A Hollywood Hills residence once owned by pioneering actress Dorothy Dandridge has returned to the luxury real estate market, carrying an asking price of
articles.body: A Hollywood Hills residence once owned by pioneering actress Dorothy Dandridge has returned to the luxury real estate market, carrying an asking price of nearly $5.5 million. The 1920s Mediterranean-style property, which combines period architectural details with contemporary upgrades, is being marketed as a home with both Hollywood history and sweeping Los Angeles views. According to Robb Report, which reported the listing on October 29, 2026, the property last changed hands in 2014 for $2.9 million. Real estate listings on Zillow and Coldwell Banker also confirm its current asking price of $5.499 million. The house, located at 1588 Viewsite Drive in the Hollywood Hills, spans approximately 4,368 square feet and has four bedrooms and five bathrooms. Its history is closely connected to Dandridge, whose achievements helped challenge racial barriers in the American film industry during the 1950s.A home with a place in Hollywood historyDandridge owned the residence between 1956 and 1963, during a period when her career had reached international prominence. Her Oscar nomination came in 1955 for her performance in Carmen Jones (1954), making her the first African American woman nominated in the Best Actress category.The milestone remains significant in Hollywood history. According to the American Film Institute, Dandridge's success with Carmen Jones also helped establish her as one of the leading Black performers of her generation. Her career, however, unfolded against an industry that continued to offer limited opportunities to Black actresses.The property reflects the architectural character of its era, with Mediterranean influences, traditional detailing and expansive windows. Among its distinctive features are stained-glass panels along the staircase, exposed wooden ceiling beams and multiple spaces designed to take advantage of the hillside setting.Inside the four-bedroom propertyThe interiors have undergone renovations while retaining several of the home's original architectural elements. A double-height entrance foyer leads into the main living area, where a carved stone fireplace serves as the focal point. The kitchen has been updated with two islands and opens into a casual sitting area and a dining space overlooking the Los Angeles skyline.Upstairs, the primary bedroom features a vaulted ceiling and French doors opening onto a balcony. Its adjoining bathroom includes a freestanding claw-foot bathtub beneath a wood-beamed ceiling. A spacious walk-in wardrobe with custom storage and a central dresser adds to the suite.The property also includes a glass-walled gym positioned above the two-car garage, as well as a separate lower-level guest area. The latter has a lounge with a wet bar, beverage refrigerators and a dishwasher, with access to an outdoor terrace featuring a built-in barbecue. Another feature that could appeal to prospective buyers is the availability of approved plans and permits for a swimming pool, offering the possibility of further developing the outdoor space.The latest listing and its price historyProperty records show that the house last sold on April 21, 2014, for $2.9 million. It was listed again on October 1, 2026, at $5.499 million, according to its real estate listing history on Compass.The current listing is being represented by Ricarda Olander of Christie's International Real Estate Southern California. The asking price represents an increase of approximately 90% over its 2014 sale price, although this does not account for renovation expenses or other ownership costs. The property's combination of architectural character, city views and celebrity history places it within a distinctive segment of the Los Angeles luxury housing market.Remembering Dorothy Dandridge's legacyBeyond its real estate appeal, the house is a reminder of an actress whose contribution to cinema extended well beyond her screen performances. Born in Cleveland, Ohio, Dandridge began performing as a child before establishing herself as an actress and singer. Her portrayal of Carmen Jones brought her international recognition, while subsequent films included Island in the Sun (1957) and Porgy and Bess (1959).She also made history as the first Black woman to appear on the cover of Life magazine in 1954 and became a prominent performer at New York's Waldorf-Astoria. Dandridge died in West Hollywood on September 8, 1965, aged 42. Her life was later brought to television in the 1999 HBO biographical film Introducing Dorothy Dandridge, starring Halle Berry.Today, the Hollywood Hills property offers prospective buyers an opportunity to own a residence associated with one of the most important trailblazers in American film history.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Martha Stewart ‘Distressed’ by Backlash to Her Homeless Halloween Costume
articles.summary: "Homelessness continues to remain one of America’s greatest challenges and ongoing crises, something that I care deeply about," entrepreneur says in statemen...
articles.body:
Martha Stewart has issued a statement after posting and then deleting a photo of herself dressed as a homeless person for Halloween.

The businesswomen and TV personality shared the photo on Instagram Saturday, showing her face dirtied, wearing ripped jeans and a torn sweater, and holding a blank clipboard that read "I Am Hungry Help Me!!" while standing with two dogs outside of a house.

The photo was included in a carousel of photos tied to her line of QVC candles. The image was quickly met with backlash online and on social media, and deleted soon after.

On Sunday, Stewart sent to a statement to Page Six saying she was "distressed" about the reaction to the photo, adding that it was meant to raise awareness to the issue and not mock it.

"I am distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people, which was never my intention," Stewart said.

"Homelessness continues to remain one of America's greatest challenges and ongoing crises, something that I care deeply about and I have spent a significant amount of time and effort supporting charities that combat this ongoing social epidemic." Stewart added that she is "committed to continuing to make a difference."

The situation hasn't kept Stewart off social media, as she was back on Instagram Sunday morning with a post about saffron .

articles.title: Michael Jackson’s sons Prince and Bigi want Neverland Ranch to help sick and underprivileged children again; owner Ron Burkle, who bought the property for $22 million in 2020, remains open to hosting charity events

articles.body: Michael Jackson’s sons, Prince and Bigi, reportedly want their late father’s famous Neverland Ranch to once again become a place where sick and underprivileged children can find happiness. The brothers hope the sprawling California estate will be preserved in a way that reflects the King of Pop’s original vision of creating a magical retreat for children.“They’d love to see the property preserved and used in a way that honors what Michael originally wanted it to be,” a source close to the Jackson family told Page Six.The insider said Neverland holds a special place in the brothers’ hearts because of the memories they made there while growing up. While Prince would particularly welcome a charitable purpose for the estate, Bigi reportedly prefers that it remain away from the spotlight rather than becoming a major tourist attraction.Prince Jackson hopes Neverland can support charitable causesPrince, 29, has continued to embrace his father's philanthropic legacy through his own charity work. He co-founded the Heal Los Angeles Foundation in 2016 while studying at Loyola Marymount University.The organisation works with children and families in underserved Los Angeles communities, focusing on education, wellness and providing support to those in need. Its initiatives include a partnership with Loreto Elementary School in northeast Los Angeles, along with food and toy drives for disadvantaged families.The foundation says its work is inspired by Michael Jackson's humanitarian legacy and his belief in giving children opportunities to succeed.“Prince really appreciates the history of Neverland and would love to see it have a charitable purpose again, especially when it comes to helping sick and underprivileged children,” the source told Page Six.“Given how involved he’s been in charity work himself, it’s something that’s particularly meaningful to him.”Bigi, formerly known as Blanket, is said to have a different approach to the property's future. According to the insider, he is more private and would not want Neverland to turn into a large tourist attraction. However, he would support efforts to bring back the happiness the estate once offered children.“Bigi is much more private and would prefer that Neverland not become some big tourist attraction, but that doesn’t mean he wouldn’t support finding a way to bring some of that magic back for children who could really benefit from it,” the source explained.The insider added that both brothers want their father's original vision to be respected.“At the end of the day, they want their father’s legacy respected, and they know how much it meant to him to create a place where kids could just be kids and forget about whatever difficulties they were going through.”Who owns Neverland Ranch after Michael Jackson's death?Despite their emotional connection to the estate, Prince and Bigi do not own Neverland or have control over its future. Businessman Ron Burkle purchased the property for approximately $22 million in 2020.A spokesperson for Burkle told Page Six that the businessman respects the estate's history and the importance it holds for the Jackson family.“Since acquiring the property, he has welcomed Michael’s children and family to spend time there whenever they wish, recognizing the personal connection they have to the home,” the spokesperson said.The statement also pointed to Burkle's history of making his private residences available for charitable events, including properties in Palm Springs, La Jolla and Green Acres.“While Neverland remains a private residence, Ron continues to welcome opportunities to host charitable events there,” the spokesperson added.Michael Jackson created Neverland as a magical retreat for childrenMichael Jackson purchased the 2,700-acre estate in Los Olivos, California, in 1988 and named it after the fictional Neverland from Peter Pan. He transformed the property into an elaborate retreat featuring amusement park rides, a train station, a movie theatre and a zoo.The singer frequently welcomed children and their families to the estate, offering them a chance to enjoy its attractions and take a break from their everyday challenges.In 1993, Michael hosted nine families through the Make-A-Wish Foundation. According to the charity's account, he personally greeted the visitors and showed them around the property.
