articles.title: 'You Can See Everything' takes lead over 'Clayface' on sleepy Halloween weekend at North American box office
articles.summary: The North American box office took a bit of a hit this weekend with the Halloween holiday drawing audiences away from theaters on Saturday.
articles.body: The North American box office took a bit of a hit this weekend with the Halloween holiday drawing audiences away from theaters on Saturday. Ticket sales were led by the Elizabeth Holmes documentary 'You Can See Everything' and the DC Studios movie 'Clayface', and aren't likely to surpass USD 56 million, according to studio estimates on Sunday. That would make it the second-lowest-earning weekend of the year.'You Can See Everything' tops box office'You Can See Everything' had the slight edge over 'Clayface', with USD 10.6 million from 2,655 locations in its third weekend in theaters. The Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim-directed film has made USD 63.9 million to date against a reported production budget of USD 7 million and continues to generate the kind of buzz that's hard to buy. This is the first time it's hit No. 1.'Clayface' scores USD 83 million globally'Clayface', about the Batman villain, trailed by only USD 200,684. The Warner Bros. release fell 57% in its second weekend in theaters. That brings its domestic earnings to USD 44.1 million against a reported USD 44 million budget. As per Variety, The film has generated USD 83 million globally.'Wildwood', 'Wicker' and 'Street Fighter' round up top 5Third place went to Laika's animated film 'Wildwood', which added 150 screens in its second weekend, bringing its footprint to 3,100 theaters in the U.S. and Canada. The Fathom Entertainment release made an estimated USD 7.5 million, down 39% from its first weekend, bringing its running total to USD 25.9 million.The comedic fantasy 'Wicker', in which Olivia Colman plays a woman who commissions a basket maker to build her a wicker husband (Alexander Skarsgard), landed in fourth place with USD 4.1 million. 'Street Fighter', now in its third weekend, rounded out the top five with USD 3.2 million.Indie films shine at box officeIn notable expansions, the acclaimed Sundance indie 'The Only Living Pickpocket in New York' added over 1,000 locations in its second weekend and made USD 1.9 million, which landed it in the top 10.Netflix also reported earnings from the theatrical release of its World War II film 'The Mosquito Bowl', which made USD 455,000 from 349 locations. articles.title: Antonelli becomes world champion as Verstappen wins in Mexico
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli becomes the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history as Max Verstappen wins the Mexico City Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli clinched his first world title and became the youngest champion in Formula 1 history by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Antonelli - 20 years and 68 days old - finished the race in third, behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

His moment of glory came on a day when tensions at Ferrari between seven-time champion Hamilton and team-mate Charles Leclerc came close to boiling over.

Antonelli drove a composed race amid some hectic action involving the other front-runners in a grand prix interrupted by a red flag that led to a 25-lap sprint to the finish.

The Italian, a teenager until late August, spent the closing laps watching Hamilton try to get close enough to pass Verstappen after the two had made contact at the first chicane at the restart.

But Hamilton found it impossible to get his Ferrari close enough to Verstappen to try to pass and ended the day frustrated and feeling a win had slipped through his fingers as a consequence of Leclerc's aggression on the first lap.

That was a secondary story on the day Antonelli made history, smashing Sebastian Vettel's previous record for being the youngest champion by three years and 67 days.

Antonelli also becomes the first Italian to win the F1 title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

Antonelli had tears mixed with laughter over the radio on the slowing down lap as he proved initially incapable of talking when his team told him he was world champion.

After he half-composed himself, he said: "Thank you so much. We did it. We did it."

Antonelli delivering the title with several races to go in a season he has taken by storm

Tension at Ferrari after Leclerc's successful attempts to grab the lead on the first lap led to controversy and unhappiness at the team

Verstappen benefiting from the internal battle to take his third win in four races.

Antonelli went into the race knowing that effectively he only had to stay out of trouble to ensure he secured the title.

The only way he could not do so was if Russell or Hamilton won the race. Even then, he needed only to finish ninth if it was his team-mate or 10th if it was Hamilton.

Antonelli ran a steady fourth in the first stint, behind Leclerc, Verstappen and Hamilton, moving into the lead as others made their pit stops in front of him, and then pitted for fresh tyres just a lap before the safety car which was why Mercedes had elongated his final stint.

A lap later, Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac crashed on lap 45 when its front suspension failed under braking for Turn One, leading initially to a safety car and then the race being stopped when it became clear how long it was going to take to repair the barriers.

At the restart, Leclerc locked his left front wheel heavily as Verstappen and Hamilton battled for the lead in front of him, and Antonelli passed him at the start of the next lap.

There was another safety car with 12 laps to go when Arvid Lindblad crashed his Racing Bulls after a collision with McLaren's Oscar Piastri.

When the race restarted with seven laps to go, Antonelli ran at the back of a three-car train with Verstappen and Hamilton, none of the three able to make any moves.

They crossed the line nose to tail, less than two seconds covering all three cars.

Hamilton left to rue race win that slipped away

The incident that is likely to lead to an inquest at Ferrari came on the first lap.

Hamilton started on pole, with Leclerc third behind Russell, but as the Mercedes dropped back Leclerc challenged Hamilton through Turns One, Two and Three.

Hamilton held him off, but at the Turn Four/Five chicane Leclerc dived around the outside before taking to the grass, cut the corner and emerged in the lead.

Hamilton had also gone off defending, although by nowhere near as much as Leclerc, and that gave Verstappen the chance to nip by Hamilton into Turn Six and into second place.

Verstappen and Hamilton both got on the radio to say Leclerc had to give the position back, but he stayed in the lead and was given a five-second penalty.

The standard punishment is 10 seconds, but the stewards took into account as mitigation that Hamilton had also gone off so neither car was in a position to make the corner.

Hamilton's argument will be that Leclerc cost him and the team a victory - had they worked together on the first lap, they could have ended it one-two and would probably have run that way to the end given the difficulty of overtaking.

Later in the race, Leclerc's lock-up after the red flag left him battling a flat spot on his tyre, and he was pressured heavily by McLaren's Lando Norris.

But despite expressing concerns about his tyre making it, he managed to hold on ahead of the 2025 world champion.

Russell took a low-key sixth, including a 10-second penalty for tipping Red Bull's Isack Hadjar into a spin on the first lap, ahead of Piastri, his car damaged in the incident with Lindblad.

articles.standfirst: Sessão de 'Divertidamente' terão audiodescrição, legendas descritivas e sinalização em Libras. Projeto chega a Brasília pelo 5º ano consecutivo e terá, ainda, oficina para educadores.
articles.summary: Sessão de 'Divertidamente' terão audiodescrição, legendas descritivas e sinalização em Libras. Projeto chega a Brasília pelo 5º ano consecutivo e terá, ainda, oficina para educadores.
articles.body:
Cena da exibição do Filme "Divertidamente" durante o Festival de Cinema Acessível Kids — Foto: Foto: Gontof Comunicação/ Divulgação

Pelo quinto ano consecutivo, o Festival de Cinema Acessível Kids fará uma sessão de cinema para crianças com necessidades especiais no Distrito Federal.

A animação "Divertida mente" (2015) será exibida com recursos específicos para crianças cegas ou com baixa visão, surdas ou com deficiência auditiva, com deficiência intelectual ou neurodivergentes.

A exibição será no Cine Brasília – que abriga a maior sala de cinema da capital federal –, com entrada gratuita.

O festival também fará uma oficina de capacitação em inclusão para educadores ( confira programação abaixo ).

Os filmes contam com r ecursos de audiodescrição, legendas descritivas e Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras) .

O projeto é parceiro do Criança Esperança e também representa uma oportunidade de acesso à cultura para famílias de baixa renda.

O Festival Acessível foi criado há 11 anos, pelo diretor de projetos de Inclusão da OSC Mais Criança Sidnei Schames. A edição infantil foi criada em 2017, após o filho de Schames, à época com 8 anos, não poder entrar na sessão do festival adulto por causa da classificação indicativa.

"Meu pai criou um festival acessível para os outros, mas não é acessível para mim", indagou o menino quando tinha 8 anos.. — Foto: Foto: Gontof Comunicação/ Divulgação

Após a criação da edição infantil, o projeto foi chancelado pela Unesco e começou a integrar o Criança Esperança, em 2022.

As oficinas de capacitação em inclusão também permitem que educadores consigam acolher crianças com deficiência e necessidades especiais. A cada turma, grupos de até 35 profissionais são capacitados.

"O projeto capacita educadores e outros profissionais para reconhecer barreiras, enfrentar preconceitos e desenvolver práticas comprometidas com a diversidade, a equidade, a acessibilidade e a inclusão. Enquanto o cinema aproxima diferentes públicos e favorece a convivência, as atividades educativas oferecem conhecimentos e instrumentos para que a experiência vivenciada continue produzindo mudanças nas escolas, nas famílias, nas instituições e nas comunidades", destaca o diretor.

Nesta edição, o festival amplia a acessibilidade das sessões para atender crianças e jovens neurodivergentes, com transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA) ou Síndrome de Down, por exemplo.

articles.title: Dustin Hoffman Says Filming ‘The Graduate’ Was a ‘Terrible Experience’ and Director Mike Nichols Made Katharine Ross Slap Him 27 Times for a Scene He ‘Didn’t Even Use’
articles.summary: Dustin Hoffman, who shot to fame after starring as Ben Braddock in Mike Nichols’ classic film “The Graduate,” has opened up about his experience shooting the...
articles.body:
Dustin Hoffman, who shot to fame after starring as Ben Braddock in Mike Nichols' classic film "The Graduate," has opened up about his experience shooting the 1967 comedy-drama in a recent essay for The New Yorker , which he described as having been a "terrible experience" despite the fact that the movie changed his life.

"I felt immediately uncomfortable, unworthy. Here I was, playing a starring role in a movie by Mike Nichols, who was the director of the moment, but I felt like I had no right to be there," writes Hoffman early in the piece of his time on set. "It was a terrible experience making the movie that changed my life." Much of his anxiety stemmed from worrying that Nichols "was angry at me, either because I was doing something wrong or because he had realized what everybody else already knew, that he had miscast the lead in his film."

Hoffman writes that the film "exacerbated all my insecurities from the start." "When my agent said that Mike was interested in me, I didn't even want to try out for the part. I had read the Charles Webb novel that Mike was adapting, and it was obvious that I was all wrong for Benjamin. A track star and straight-A student, the head of the debate team—this was an affluent, all-American kid, whose surname was 'Braddock.' Why would you cast a person who looks as ethnic as I do to play the ultimate Wasp? It made absolutely no sense." He continued, explaining that his agent convinced him to screen-test for the role, which he ultimately got.

However, beyond Hoffman's worries about his ability to play Ben, he also writes that Nichols was "frequently sour" on set, a "shocking, destabilizing" change from his personality during rehearsals. "I often felt that I was about to be fired. When we were shooting some of the film's most famous sequences, I remember thinking, I have no fucking idea what I'm doing," said Hoffman.

He also notes that while the director was "irritable with everyone," there was a "certain sadism" that "seemed to creep in" only with him.

He continued: "There was a scene in which Katharine Ross had to slap me, and he made us do twenty-seven takes. The scene has Benjamin run into Elaine's room, soaking wet from the rain, to tell her that he's had an affair with an older woman; within seconds, Elaine realizes the woman is her mother. Mike just kept telling Katharine to hit me, to hit me harder. Katharine worried she would hurt me, and I told her, 'I'm O.K. Just don't hit my ear.' Unfortunately, she missed a few times. I was dizzy by the end of that day, and Mike didn't even use the slap in the film."

The following day, Hoffman shot an underwater scene that required him to stay submerged in a scuba suit. "When I came up for air after a few takes, there was blood trickling out of my ear. Between all the slapping during the previous day and all the water pressure at the bottom of the pool, I'd punctured an eardrum," he writes.

"The Graduate" first hit theaters on Dec. 22, 1967. It was nominated for seven Oscars and won for best picture at the 40th Academy Awards.

articles.title: Chris Pratt went from living in a van to Hollywood stardom after chance encounter changed everything
articles.summary: Chris Pratt recalls the moment Rae Dawn Chong walked into Bubba Gump Shrimp Company and offered him a role that launched his Hollywood career.
articles.body: Chris Pratt's journey to becoming one of Hollywood's go-to action stars started with him living in a van in Hawaii. In a recent post on X, the 47-year-old actor reflected on his beginnings: "Before Hollywood, I was living in a van in Hawaii and waiting tables at Bubba Gump Shrimp Company," revealing that a chance encounter working one night changed his life. "One day, the incredible Rae Dawn Chong walked into the restaurant, and naturally, I went up to her table and said, 'Hey, you’re a movie star! What are you doing here?'" he recalled. "She asked if I could act, and I said, 'F- - - yeah, put me in your movie!'" Since he didn't have a phone, he gave Chong his friend Mike's number, who told him a few days later that someone had called for him. NICKI MINAJ, ANNA NICOLE SMITH AND MORE STARS WHO GOT THEIR START WAITING TABLES AT RED LOBSTER "I called her back, and sure enough, she was serious," he wrote. "I drove over to pick up the script, went back to Mike’s house, and read all 120 pages three times in a row. First script I’d ever read. My character's name was Devon, and I remember thinking, 'Sweet! I could totally play a Devon!' After the audition, he recalled Chung telling him he "could act and offered me the part." While he lived in Hawaii, the movie was filming in Los Angeles, which made Pratt a little nervous, as he had "about $60 to my name, a bag of clothes, and some rollerblades." He then found out that Chung would fly him out to Los Angeles for production. "I remember thinking right then and there, my life just changed forever. I'm going to be an actor," he wrote. "That little movie was 'Cursed Part 3,' a low-budget horror comedy that opened the door to Hollywood for me. I'll forever be grateful to Rae for taking a chance on a kid working at a shrimp restaurant. Everybody starts somewhere, and this is where it all began for me." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Pratt's role in "Cursed Part 3" led to bigger projects, including his breakout role playing Andy Dwyer in the hit NBC show, "Parks and Recreation." He then landed the role of Peter Quill, or Star-Lord, in the Marvel movie, "Guardians of the Galaxy," playing the character in the film's two sequels, as well as in "Avengers: Infinity War" and "Avengers: Endgame." When speaking to Moviefone in May 2023, Pratt shared he is "grateful" for "Guardians of the Galaxy" director James Gunn for casting him as the lead in the movie, saying, "He's changed my life" and the life of his children. "He found a working actor who had already at that point done way better than most people who come out to town. I wasn't a waiter any longer, I was a series regular on a show. I was getting recognition," he said. "He brought me to a whole new level that ultimately changed the entire way the industry saw me. I no longer was auditioning. articles.title: Annu Kapoor criticizes Naseeruddin Shah over 'Dimagi Naxal' remark: 'I have serious reservations about people who make such statements'
articles.summary: Veteran actor Annu Kapoor has questioned Naseeruddin Shah's views on India's interests following the latter's recent 'Dimagi Naxal' remark.
articles.body: Veteran actor Annu Kapoor has questioned Naseeruddin Shah's views on India's interests following the latter's recent 'Dimagi Naxal' remark.The discussion began after Naseeruddin Shah shared a video on Tuesday supporting students of Delhi's Jamia Millia Islamia. The students have been protesting to demand the restoration of their student union. Shah appeared in the video wearing a badge with the words 'Dimagi Naxal'.Annu Kapoor questions Naseeruddin Shah's 'Dimagi Naxal' statementSpeaking to ANI, Annu expressed doubts about how seriously Naseeruddin considers the country's interests and welfare. He said, "He may be good at delivering dialogues, but I doubt how much he genuinely thinks about the country's interests and welfare. I have serious reservations about people who make such statements. It is our democracy that allows them to speak freely, make such statements and hold protests."Naseeruddin Shah supports Jamia Millia Islamia studentsThe controversy followed a video in which Naseeruddin Shah extended his support to students and said, "I proudly declare that I am Dimagi Naxal. I don't know what other nicknames the watchmen have given to people like me, anti-national, tukde tukde gang, and I don't know what else."Shah has also used his social media platforms to support student demonstrations in recent months. His recent interventions include expressing solidarity with students protesting at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) in Kolkata last week.Ashoke Pandit accuses Naseeruddin Shah of repeatedly using abusive languageFilmmaker Ashoke Pandit has joined the criticism, expressing strong disapproval of Shah's recent remarks. He alleged, "I'm not shocked, nor am I surprised by Naseeruddin Shah's abusive language because, since the last few months, in fact for a year, he has been constantly misbehaving and has become a compulsive abuser. The kind of language which he uses, the way he distorts his face, he exposes his frustration. There are reasons behind it, I can understand, and I pity him. When I see him totally distorted, totally frustrated on camera, and he's trying to vent out his frustration, the more he vents out his frustration, the more he is getting exposed day by day, every day."'The Kashmir Files', 'The Kerala Story' and 'Dhurandhar' enter the debateAshoke Pandit also connected his criticism to the reception of certain commercially successful Hindi films. He suggested that the narratives explored in these projects might be among the reasons behind Shah's reactions. The filmmaker said, "Probably one of the reasons why he's feeling insecure is that the films which are doing well in the in the in the country is not suiting him. Films like Kashmir Files, Kerala Story, Dhurandhar. These narratives are not suiting them. They're suffering from an inferiority complex. Hence, this is kind of behaviour with which he's trying to come out. So I think, in the end, I would like to tell him that he should consult a psychiatrist because it's affecting his mental health. articles.title: 'RC17': Anirudh Ravichander to compose music for Ram Charan's film after rumoured exit from Shah Rukh Khan's 'King'
articles.summary: Ram Charan and director Sukumar have officially kick-started their second collaboration with the launch of their upcoming film, tentatively titled 'RC17'.
articles.body: Ram Charan and director Sukumar have officially kick-started their second collaboration with the launch of their upcoming film, tentatively titled 'RC17'. The project was inaugurated with a grand pooja ceremony in Hyderabad on November 1, 2026. Megastar Chiranjeevi attended the event and sounded the clapboard, marking the formal beginning of the production. Meanwhile, a major update about the film's music has emerged, with composer Anirudh Ravichander reportedly coming on board.According to Variety, Anirudh Ravichander has joined the project as its music composer. This marks his first collaboration with Sukumar and another association with Ram Charan after their earlier plans to work together on 'Bruce Lee: The Fighter' did not materialise, owing to scheduling conflicts. The development is particularly interesting as Sukumar has traditionally worked with Devi Sri Prasad on most of his films.Anirudh Ravichander joins Ram Charan's 'RC17'Ravichander's association with 'RC17' now marks the first time Anirudh Ravichander will work with Sukumar and Ram Charan together. The filmmaker has maintained a long-standing professional association with Devi Sri Prasad, who has composed music for several of his directorial ventures.Anirudh Ravichander reportedly exits Shah Rukh Khan's 'King'Meanwhile, Ravichander was in the news over his rumoured exit from Shah Rukh Khan's King. According to a report by Bollywood Hungama, he amicably stepped away from 'King' because of his packed professional schedule. A source quoted in the report stated that the composer could not dedicate the time required for a film of this scale. However, he has reportedly gifted Shah Rukh a theme track for the project, which is scheduled for a Christmas release.Chiranjeevi gives the first clap at 'RC17' launchThe launch ceremony brought together several prominent members of the Telugu film industry. Ram Charan arrived at the venue and greeted the team before taking part in the traditional proceedings. A video shared by the production team captured moments from the event, which began at approximately 10:50 am.Chiranjeevi performed the ceremonial coconut-breaking ritual and sounded the clapboard for the film. Sharing a glimpse of the occasion, the makers wrote, “The journey of #RC17 begins with the MEGA CLAP Megastar @KChiruTweets garu sounded the clapboard and blessed the entire team of #RC17.”The event was attended by Sukumar and his wife, Ravi Shankar, Naveen Yerneni, Naga Vamsi, Rahul Sankrityan, Gopichand Malineni, Maruthi, Buchi Babu Sana, Vamsi Nandipati and Harish Shankar, among others.The project was first announced in March 2024. Ram Charan shared a photograph with Sukumar during the Holi celebrations, confirming that the actor and filmmaker were reuniting. Their upcoming film marks their first collaboration since the 2018 blockbuster 'Rangasthalam'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Naslen gets emotional at 'Scene' event; praises Suriya's hard work and kindness: 'Every day during the shoot, Suriya sir would send me food'
articles.summary: Malayalam actor Naslen is set to make his Tamil debut with Suriya's upcoming film 'Scene'.
articles.body: Malayalam actor Naslen is set to make his Tamil debut with Suriya's upcoming film 'Scene'. Directed by Jithu Madhavan, the film is scheduled to release in theatres on November 6. The actor has already received a warm welcome from Tamil audiences, even before the film's release. His speech at the film's recent event in Chennai became one of the evening's highlights. Naslen shared how he worked with Suriya, the affection he got from the team, and the lessons he learnt while shooting the movie.Naslen thanks Tamil fans and shares his excitement about 'Scene'Speaking at the 'Scene' event, Naslen became emotional while discussing the response to his first Tamil film. He said, "I haven't acted in any Tamil film before this. This is my first Tamil film, but you have already given me so much love. It feels very emotional. The film is releasing on November 6, and I hope you continue to show me the same love after watching it." He also spoke about his love for Tamil food and added, "I like Pongal among Tamil Nadu's food items." His simple words received a warm response from the audience. The actor also apologised for his Tamil, saying that he was still learning the language.Naslen praises Suriya's hard work and kindness during 'Scene' shootingNaslen also shared a special memory from the film's shooting and spoke about Suriya's kindness towards him. He said, "Every day during the shoot, Suriya sir would send me food in his lunch box for both lunch and dinner. His love was also part of that food." The actor further praised Suriya's dedication to his work. "One thing I learned from Suriya sir is that he is a very hardworking person. He is interested in everything he does," Naslen said. He added that Suriya's attitude towards work left a strong impression on him.Naslen says Suriya's dedication inspires young actorsTalking about the shooting schedule, Naslen revealed that the team often worked from 6 pm to 6 am. Though it was an exhausting schedule, Suriya kept himself fresh and continued with his other commitments as well. Naslen said, "Once the shooting is over, even though we will be mentally exhausted, even then, he would be fresh and energetic." He added that such dedication was inspiring for actors at the beginning of their careers.
